properties.name: adopt's instructions never mention nesting — no contain_component, no depth guidance — and every design it produced is FLAT: dev_storyflow 101 components with ZERO containing another, mapwright 15 with zero. The hierarchy is observable in the source and adopt does not recover it
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25, closing a line of investigation that had been reading the symptom as a user preference.

⚠️ PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY — READ THE NOTE AT THE FOOT BEFORE QUOTING THE HEADLINE. Left OPEN rather than closed, because only half of it moved.

ANTHONY'S FRAMING, which is what made the measurement possible: *"if I gave you the adopt task for storyflow, you should be able to see all the services (roughly equal to a subsystem). then inspect inside each service to see all the different scripts (getting into components) and then probably into the individual function and classes to determine the sub-component level and so on. **the hierarchy is there.**"*

── WHAT ADOPT ACTUALLY INSTRUCTS ──
`getting-started/skills/adopt/SKILL.md` grepped for every hierarchy word: **`contain_component` ZERO times. `nest` zero. `parent` zero. `subsystem` zero. `depth` zero.** `hierarchy_issues` appears ONCE, as a detector to run afterwards — so the skill checks a spine it never tells anyone to build. `level` appears once, in unrelated prose about test levels.

── WHAT ADOPT PRODUCED, measured across four designs ──

    design            components   containing another component
    dev_storyflow (ajs77)   101          0
    dev_storyflow (local)    84          0
    mapwright                15          0
    music_graph              25          2

⇒ **EVERY ADOPTED DESIGN IS FLAT.** dev_storyflow puts 101 components directly under the Project — and 10 of them declare `subsystem` or `system`, so the design CLAIMS a hierarchy that structurally does not exist. Contrast flo2, the only design in the sample shaped by genesis rather than adopt: 12 components, depth 3, fan-out 6/2/2/1/1, zero span-of-control violations.

⭐⭐ THE FLATNESS IS A SKILL DEFECT, NOT A USER PREFERENCE, AND THAT INVERTS AN EARLIER READING. Measurements taken hours before were read as "real designs are two rungs deep, so nobody needs depth" — with the caveat that it might be the absence of instruction. It is the absence of instruction: the systems adopt was pointed at HAVE observable hierarchies (storyflow's services ▸ scripts ▸ functions/classes), and adopt walks past them.

── WHY THIS IS A GAP IN ADOPT AND NOT A FAILURE OF THE IDEA ──
`dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` (ACCEPTED 2026-07-23, derived with the user) already drew the line Anthony redrew today: *"A functional carving comes from the product's PURPOSE (a genesis input), not the code, and cuts across crate boundaries, so **adopt on the code can only re-derive the module view.**"* That is right and it is NOT an excuse for flatness. The module view is itself hierarchical — package ▸ module ▸ class — and recovering it is exactly what adopt is for. Adopt cannot produce the FUNCTIONAL carving; it can and should produce the STRUCTURAL one.

📌 AND A SECOND, RELATED GAP MEASURED EARLIER AND STILL OPEN: of 178 `ALLOCATED_TO` edges on reflow2's own design, **177 point at a leaf MODULE and exactly ONE at a subsystem**; `DECOMPOSES` is zero. Doctrine allocates functions at EACH level as it decomposes — functions to the system, then to subsystems, then to components. reflow2 records allocation at one level only, and the per-subsystem function counts are computed by walking CONTAINS rather than being stated. Anthony's own description of the process — *"you allocate functions to a system, then within a system allocate functions into subsystems or components and so on"* — is not recordable today.

⚠️ BOUNDS: four adopted designs, all produced by the same person with the same agent, so this measures how THIS adopt is followed rather than how it must be. The skill text is the stronger evidence — an instruction that is absent cannot be followed inconsistently. Nothing here says what the right depth for storyflow is; it says adopt never asked.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🔻 PARTIAL SUPERSESSION — 2026-08-25, LATER THE SAME DAY (PR #335, merged as 323d11f)
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**THE FIRST HALF IS NOW FALSE. THE SECOND HALF IS STILL TRUE.** Nothing above has been altered; this section is added beside it, because a closed measurement is evidence and an erased one is a hole.

❌ **FALSE AS OF #335:** *"adopt's instructions never mention nesting — `contain_component` ZERO times, no depth guidance."* PR #335 added a nesting step to Phase 1 of the adopt skill, in all three mirrors. One bullet, no code — `contain_component`, `Component.level` and `hierarchy_issues` all already existed and worked; the only thing missing was the instruction. **Re-grepping the skill today would contradict the paragraph above, which is why this note exists.**

✅ **STILL TRUE, and untouched by #335:** the four measured designs remain flat — nobody has re-adopted dev_storyflow, mapwright or music_graph, so 101/0, 84/0, 15/0 and 25/2 all still stand. The counterfactual run before the edit recovered depth `{1:1, 2:5, 3:73, 4:2}` on a SCRATCH graph only. **An instruction added is not a design re-derived.**

✅ **ALSO STILL TRUE:** the second gap in the 📌 paragraph — allocation recorded at one level only, `DECOMPOSES` zero. #335 did not touch it.

🛑 **NOT CLOSED, AND DELIBERATELY.** `valid_to` asserts the WHOLE thing stopped being true, and the measurement of what adopt PRODUCED is the durable half. It becomes closable when some real system is re-adopted under the new instruction and the component/nesting counts are taken again — that measurement has not been made, and claiming it would be exactly the false-green this project exists to prevent.
